summary: Zijie Li works in Buddhist studies. Li studied at Komazawa University and held a post at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science as 特別研究員DC.
Zong Rinpoche (1905–1984) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Trijang Rinpoche and held a post at Ganden Shartse Monastery from circa 1937 to 1946.

Zongsan Mou (1909–1995) worked in philosophy and sinology. He studied under Shili Xiong (~1928–1933) and at Peking University (~1929–1933), later holding posts at Zhejiang, National Taiwan, National Taiwan Normal, Tunghai, and the New Asia Institute (~1974–1995).

Zsóka Gelle is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Vienna in 2011. She held posts at Eötvös Loránd University (2014–2016), Budapest Centre for Buddhist Studies (2014–2016), Tibet House Foundation, and East-West Research Institute.

Zuiei Ito (1942–2020) specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1965–1970) and held posts at Rissho University (~1976–2012 as 仏教学科教授), the University of Tokyo, and Waseda University.

Zuiho Yamaguchi (1926–2023) studied at the University of Tokyo, under Rolf Alfred Stein, and Jacques Bacot in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Toyo Bunko (~1964–1978), the University of Tokyo (1970–1986), and Nagoya University (~1987–1990).

Zuiryu Nakamura (1915–1997) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Rissho University (~1937–1940) and under Susumu Yamaguchi and Kenryu Tsukinowa. In 1945, he became Professor of the Department of Buddhist Studies at Rissho University.

Édouard Chavannes (1865–1918) was a sinology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at École Normale Supérieure (~1885–1888). He served as a professor at Collège de France from 1893 to 1918.

Édouard Huber (1879–1914) worked in sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Paris, École nationale des langues orientales vivantes, and Collège de France, and was Professeur p. i. de chinois at EFEO (~1905–1914).

Émile Benveniste (1902–1976) specialized in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Paris and under Antoine Meillet, later holding posts at École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1927–1969) and Collège de France (1937–1972).

Émile Burnouf (1821–1907) specialized in Indology and linguistics. He studied at École Normale Supérieure, French School at Athens, and under Jean-Louis and Eugène Burnouf, later holding professorial posts at Faculté des lettres de Nancy and University of Nancy (1854–1867).

Émile Senart (1847–1928) worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. He studied under Theodor Benfey (~1867–1868) and held posts as Professor at the University of Strasbourg and President of the Société Asiatique (1908–1928).

Étienne Balázs (1905–1963) worked in sinology and history/archaeology. He studied under Otto Franke in 1923, became 主任研究員 at the CNRS in 1949, and served as 中國經濟史主任教授 at the University of Paris (~1955–1963).

Étienne Lamotte (1903–1983) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at KU Leuven, Sapienza, Paris, INALCO, EPHE, and Collège de France. He held posts at KU Leuven, Université catholique de Louvain, and the Royal Academy of Belgium.

Ñāṇavīra Thera (1920–1965) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Magdalene College (~1938–1940) and under Pelene Siri Vajirañāṇa (~1949–1950), and served in the Royal Artillery (1939–1941) and Intelligence Corps (1941–1945).

Ülo Valk (born 1962) specializes in religious studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Tartu (~1981–1986), where he held a post circa 1991, and served as an editor for Numen (~2004–2012).
